newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on heavy selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on heavy selling.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down in active trading on Thursday with heavy selling triggered by overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,040 yuan ($2,412) per tonne, losing 330 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,370 and hit a low of 19,900.

September fell 220 to 21,010, October 180 to 20,600, November 210 to 20,340, December 350 to 20,050, the February 1997 contract 340 to 20,050, March 370 to 20,050, April 300 to 20,100 and May rose 30 to 20,480.
Combined volume rocketed to 85,580 tonnes from 15,060.
Copper opened sharply down. Short-covering and speculative buying pushed the prices off their lows but they still ended lower than Wednesday's close.

Traders said copper breached the key $1,900 support level on the LME on Wednesday and this triggered heavy selling in Shanghai today. They expect Shanghai copper futures to continue to fall on Friday if the LME loses tonight.
"Panic stop-loss orders from retail investors were responsible for today's sharp falls," said one trader.
"But all late-maturing contracts found strong support at the 20,000-yuan level, indicating speculative buying emerged at low levels," he added.
"Copper will fall further in the next few days with large amounts of stop-loss orders expected to emerge if the key 20,000-yuan support level is breached," said a second trader.
"Market fundamentals are very poor," he added.
Aluminium ended down across the board. September fell 30 to 13,950, October 150 to 14,000 and November 170 to 13,950.
Combined volume fell to 1,340 tonnes form 1,900.
